objects.name: Woolly mammoth skeleton
objects.fact: Woolly mammoths roamed the cold steppes of the last Ice Age. A small population survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago.

objects.name: 1903 Wright Flyer
objects.fact: The first powered, controlled airplane. Its first flight at Kitty Hawk on December 17, 1903 lasted 12 seconds.

objects.name: Bell X-1 "Glamorous Glennis"
objects.fact: On October 14, 1947, Chuck Yeager flew it faster than the speed of sound, the first airplane ever to do so.

objects.name: Space Shuttle Discovery
objects.fact: Discovery flew more missions than any other shuttle, including the 1990 launch of the Hubble Space Telescope.

objects.name: Apollo 11 Command Module "Columbia"
objects.fact: Columbia carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins to the Moon and back. It was the only part of the spacecraft to return to Earth.

objects.name: Apollo 11 crew hatch
objects.fact: The main hatch on Columbia. This "unified hatch" was redesigned after the 1967 Apollo 1 fire so crews could get out quickly.

objects.name: Morse-Vail telegraph key
objects.fact: Made by Alfred Vail and believed to be from the first Baltimore–Washington telegraph line, demonstrated in 1844.

objects.name: Charlie Parker’s alto saxophone
objects.hint: African American History and Culture Museum · c. 1947
objects.fact: Charlie "Bird" Parker’s sax, with a sterling silver bell engraved with his name, made around 1947.

objects.name: Triceratops skeleton ("Hatcher")
objects.fact: Hatcher was the first Triceratops ever put on display, and the first whole dinosaur skeleton the Smithsonian scanned in 3D.
